title: Buffalo Chicken Dip
subtitle: Spicy dip, chips, zero utensils
description: Spicy dip, chips, zero utensils. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Fold the buffalo dip
steps.instruction: Mix cream cheese, hot sauce, ranch, and chicken until smooth. Spread in a buttered baking dish; top with cheddar.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 20–25 minutes until edges bubble and center reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes — molten cheese burns tongues.

steps.title: Serve with chips
steps.instruction: Serve hot with chips and celery. Hold in a slow cooker on warm — do not reheat cold dip in microwave (greasy separation).

steps.title: Refresh the dip
steps.instruction: Stir dip between waves of eaters. If skin forms on top, fold it in — add a splash of hot sauce if it tastes flat.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Buffalo Chicken Dip with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Build a long snack board: mains down the center, dips and chips at both ends.
Use disposable boats for handhelds so cleanup stays under five minutes after the game.
Line up Buffalo Chicken Dip on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Spicy dip, chips, zero utensils. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
